name: EGCG

lead: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) is the most abundant catechin in green tea and a polyphenol with antioxidant properties. It is sold as a concentrated extract in fat-burner and weight-management products, typically alongside caffeine.
Trials and meta-analyses of green tea catechins on weight and fat mass show small effects at best, with inconsistent results and strong dependence on caffeine intake and baseline habits.

paras: EGCG may modestly raise energy expenditure and fat oxidation by inhibiting catechol-O-methyltransferase, which prolongs noradrenaline signalling, and may reduce fat absorption in the gut. Its effects in cells involve many pathways, but these have not translated to clear clinical results in people.

Concentrated green tea extracts, especially taken on an empty stomach, have been linked to liver injury in rare cases, and the European Food Safety Authority has set a caution level for catechin intake from supplements. EGCG can also reduce the absorption of iron and interact with some drugs. It is sold as a supplement; beverage tea is considered safe.
